definitions.gloss: religious precepts; commandments; moral or religious rules
definitions.explanation: Rules of conduct prescribed by a religion, particularly the disciplinary rules observed by Buddhist monks and nuns, or more broadly, any set of religious commandments.

examples.japanese: ⟦{僧侶|そうりょ}→僧侶：11529_souryo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{厳|きび}しい→厳しい：01125_kibishii⟧{戒律|かいりつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{守|まも}る→守る：01986_mamoru⟧。
⟦その→その：00993_sono⟧⟦{宗教|しゅうきょう}→宗教：03208_shuukyou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{食事|しょくじ}→食事：02087_shokuji⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{関|かん}する→関する：02045_kansuru⟧{戒律|かいりつ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: That religion has precepts concerning food.

examples.japanese: {戒律|かいりつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{破|やぶ}った→破る：02321_yaburu⟧⟦{僧侶|そうりょ}→僧侶：11529_souryo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{寺|てら}→寺：01676_tera⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{追放|ついほう}→追放：14313_tsuihou⟧⟦された→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The monk who broke the precepts was expelled from the temple.

notes:
Composed of {戒|かい} (admonition, precept) + {律|りつ} (law, rule). Originally a Buddhist term: {戒|かい} refers to moral rules one voluntarily accepts, while {律|りつ} refers to rules imposed by the monastic community. Together they encompass the full body of religious discipline.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {戒律|かいりつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{守|まも}る→守る：01986_mamoru⟧ — to observe/keep religious precepts
- {戒律|かいりつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{破|やぶ}る→破る：02321_yaburu⟧ — to break religious precepts
- ⟦{厳|きび}しい→厳しい：01125_kibishii⟧{戒律|かいりつ} — strict precepts
- {戒律|かいりつ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{従|したが}う→従う：02059_shitagau⟧ — to follow religious precepts

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{教|おし}え→教え：01909_oshie⟧ — teachings (more general; any religious or moral teaching)
- ⟦{掟|おきて}→掟：12706_okite⟧ — rules, code (secular or religious rules of a group)
- {十戒|じっかい} — the Ten Commandments
- {五戒|ごかい} — the Five Precepts (basic Buddhist ethical guidelines)

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japanese Buddhism, the {五戒|ごかい} (Five Precepts) — not to kill, steal, lie, commit sexual misconduct, or consume intoxicants — are the most widely known. However, the strictness of observance varies greatly among Japanese Buddhist sects.
